name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing, inauthentic networks, and deceptive information operations across Facebook, Instagram and other platforms, including the CooRnet/CLSB methodology and its applications to elections, gambling promotion and cross-national disinformation campaigns. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution and the throughline of vera.ai WP4, PROMPT-adjacent work, and multiple recent case studies (Nigeria, India, Germany, Brazil, Italy).

name: Information Disorder & Misinformation
description: Conceptual and empirical work on fake news, disinformation and problematic information circulating in hybrid media systems, spanning taxonomy-building, fact-checking support (MINE-FACTS), and monitoring of sensitive narratives (Ukraine war, health, elections) under projects like PROMPT. A core, long-running theme that anchors the researcher's identity as an information-disorder scholar.

name: Platform Data Access & Governance
description: Research on the shifting infrastructure of platform-mediated research after CrowdTangle's shutdown and the DSA-era API landscape, alongside studies of Meta's content-moderation and political-content policies (e.g. Political Content Reduction Policy, the 100-public-shares URL dataset threshold). Reflects an active concern with how platform governance decisions constrain and reshape social media research methods.

name: Computational Methods & LLMs for Content Analysis
description: Methodological work on integrating large language models and embedding models into political discourse and communication research pipelines, including validation of LLMs-in-the-loop annotation, human-machine disagreement, and comparative embedding evaluation for clustering political news. A rapidly growing, current strand tied to the researcher's PhD/Master teaching in generative AI.

name: Generative AI & Media Manipulation
description: Investigation of how generative AI is used to produce and evolve deceptive visual and textual content in coordinated influence operations (e.g. AI-generated gambling promotion imagery), and broader concern with countering disinformation in the generative-AI era. Directly connected to the new 'IA Generativa e Media' course and the researcher's most recent publications.

name: Political Communication & Elections
description: Studies of social media dynamics around electoral campaigns (Italian 2018/2019/2022, German 2021, Brazilian post-Bolsonaro), including partisan attention, affective polarization, insularity, and cross-partisan news engagement. A long-standing empirical anchor of the MINE program that continues to generate active output.

name: MINE — Mapping Italian News Program
description: The institutional and intellectual umbrella coordinated by the researcher since 2017, hosting successive externally funded sub-projects on Italian media coverage, social media's role in elections, public opinion and health information. Remains the organizing structure for the whole research agenda even though individual grants have concluded.

name: Health Misinformation & Digital Gatekeeping
description: Research on the circulation of problematic health content and its drivers on social media in cross-national contexts (India, Nigeria, COVID-19 Italy), and on the gatekeeping role of platforms like Google News in shaping health information exposure. Connects earlier Gates Foundation-funded work to ongoing interest in health-related information ecosystems.

name: Sociocybernetics & Social Systems Theory
description: A recurring theoretical thread applying Luhmannian social systems theory and sociocybernetics to understand digital media, political crises, and complexity in contemporary societies, reflecting the researcher's doctoral roots and ongoing engagement with ISA's Research Committee on Sociocybernetics.

name: Public and Sociotechnical Approaches to AI Safety Evaluation
description: Papers framing AI safety practices—red-teaming and evaluation—as sociotechnical activities requiring public involvement, labor consideration, and participatory science methods rather than purely technical procedures.

name: Online Radicalization and Extremism Across Platforms
description: Empirical and review studies of how extremist actors (far-right, jihadist) exploit platform affordances, algorithms, and multimodal content to spread and normalize radical ideologies online.

name: Retrospective Essays on Platformization and Social Media's Trajectory
description: Reflective anniversary/position essays diagnosing the current state of social media and platform economies, tracing how platformization, political economy, and scam/extractive logics have reshaped online life over the past decade.

name: Public Attitudes and Labor Experiences with AI
description: Survey- and discourse-based studies of how publics and workers perceive, use, and are shaped by AI systems, including stakeholder discourse, national attitudes, and worker-reported productivity and displacement effects.

name: LLMs and Computational Methods for Research Workflows
description: Methodological papers deploying LLMs or fine-tuned models to augment scholarly tasks such as peer review, qualitative coding, and domain-specific classification, with attention to human-in-the-loop design and evaluation.

name: Message-Based Interventions for Climate Communication and Misinformation Resistance
description: Experimental and review studies testing how framed messages, chatbots, or inoculation techniques shape audience attitudes, resistance to misinformation, and engagement with climate or conspiracy content.

name: Survey Data Quality, Comprehension, and Recruitment
description: Papers examining the methodological foundations of online survey research, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how representative and valid different opt-in sample sources are, and how novel platform-based recruitment strategies (e.g., Facebook ads) can be used and evaluated for reaching hard-to-survey populations.

name: Computational Approaches to Social Network Structure and Community Formation
description: Papers developing or applying computational/graph-based methods to detect, map, and explain emergent structural patterns—communities, practice clusters, and transitive ties—in large-scale online social networks, using techniques such as self-supervised graph embeddings and causal network analysis.

name: Cultural Imaginaries and Framings of Generative AI
description: Papers examining how generative AI is culturally imagined, discursively framed, and theorized as a medium, ranging from newspaper coverage and Silicon Valley community discourse to media-theoretical accounts of AI's distinctive properties as a creative medium.
